basis: Calcification of dental pulp; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Autoimmune disorder of neuronal inhibition; spasms and rigidity reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic muscle damage.
ODAPH-related defective dental enamel maturation; no established extraoral organ damage.
Hereditary colorectal cancer; additional cancer susceptibilities do not establish damage to other organs.
Fragile X syndrome subtype; the parent establishes a neurodevelopmental disorder. No evidence supports additional damaged organs.
Carcinoma originating in the breast, which has no axis.
Congenital femoral deficiency with impaired hip and knee mobility.
Isolated abnormal ferritin/hepcidin regulation; elevated circulating markers do not establish hepatic injury or blood-cell disease.
Ischemic injury of the posterior optic nerve; optic nerve disease belongs to the ocular axis. Arteritis is only one possible cause.
Progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with profound developmental impairment and seizures; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Marrow crowding: anemia 3/6, thrombocytopenia 2/5; optic compression: visual impairment 2/5; hypocalcemia 3/6. Hepatomegaly reflects extramedullary hematopoiesis.
Corneal inflammation; neither an infectious nor an autoimmune cause is established for this concept.
Fragile X neurodevelopmental syndrome; no additional common organ damage is established for this record.
Neurodegeneration and cutaneous photosensitivity define the syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss 30-79%. Atherosclerosis is a separate disease; vascular calcification may not impair function.
Iron-overload liver disease is defining; hepatomegaly 3/6. Neurodegeneration and dermatitis/ichthyosis define syndrome; dental changes 50-67%, hearing loss 2/6, contractures 2/6 omitted by cap.
Unregulated pancreatic insulin secretion causes persistent hypoglycemia; hypoglycemic brain injury with lasting developmental impairment affects approximately 30-50%.
Cartilage dysplasia and pulmonary artery stenosis define disease; airway malformation/calcification 80-99%, hearing loss 12/17. Developmental impairment 10/17 omitted by cap.
Schwann-cell neoplasm arising from peripheral nerve sheaths; cellular morphology does not establish another organ of origin.
Tuberculous infection of the heart, pericardium or vessels; pulmonary involvement is not required by this extrapulmonary concept.
Acquired factor IX inhibition by autoantibodies causes a coagulation disorder; bleeding sites do not define additional commonly damaged organs.
Severe intellectual disability and megalencephaly with defining kyphoscoliosis and skeletal overgrowth; facial and orbital morphology do not establish ocular damage.
Congenital atresia of the coronary venous drainage structure.
Immune cryoglobulin-mediated vasculitis; many patients are asymptomatic. Persistent skin, renal or nerve damage is not established in >=30% across this umbrella.
Viral infection causes myocardial damage and dilated cardiomyopathy.
Melanoma of the retina; ocular origin determines the axis. Metastatic risks do not establish other organ involvement.
